subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What identity should OpenClaw use as the canonical inbound-media isolation boundary for multi-agent deployments?
rationale: The source problem is clear, but choosing agent id, channel account id, session/chat scope, or a tenant/account hierarchy changes the security boundary, compatibility behavior, and plugin SDK contract.

options.title: Agent-scoped contract
options.body: Scope inbound media by resolved agent id after routing, preserving the documented agent isolation model but requiring media provenance to survive early channel ingest.

options.title: Account-scoped ingest contract
options.body: Scope by channel account id at save time, which is easier for current monitors but only approximates agent isolation when accounts and agents are not one-to-one.

options.title: Tenant/chat/session hierarchy
options.body: Design a richer namespace such as tenant/account/chat/session before implementation, which may solve more provenance needs but is broader and slower to land.

recommendation.title: Agent-scoped contract
recommendation.body: Scope inbound media by resolved agent id after routing, preserving the documented agent isolation model but requiring media provenance to survive early channel ingest.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the core media reference, sandbox staging, and Discord media surfaces plus the prior maintainer review context.
